title: Register: formal vs informal
note: the register choice itself · phrasal verb vs single Latinate verb (put off/postpone, find out/discover, look into/investigate) · formal prepositional phrases (prior to, owing to, in the event of, in accordance with, on behalf of, with a view to) including despite as a preposition · the fixed correspondence frames and the look forward to + -ing trap · formal degree (considerably, somewhat, particularly) plus the countable/uncountable split in a great deal of vs a large number of · deliberately avoids ground owned elsewhere: inverted conditionals (c1_inversion_emphasis), impersonal it is said (c1_advanced_passive), situational ellipsis and particles (c1_spoken_vs_written), formal connectors (b2_discourse_markers), fronted preposition + whom (b2_relative_clauses_advanced) · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 15)

items.en: The meeting has been postponed until June.
items.cz: Schůzka byla odložena na červen.
items.gap: The meeting has been ____ until June.
accepts: The meeting has been postponed until June.
items.explanation: The single clearest register signal in English is the choice between a phrasal verb and a single Latinate one. Put off and postpone mean the same thing; find out and discover mean the same thing; but one belongs to speech and to writing that wants to sound like speech, and the other belongs to a report, a contract or a letter to someone you have not met. Neither is better English. What is wrong is mixing them — a formal letter that says we put off the meeting, or a conversation that says I shall investigate it. Czech marks the same distance with word choice too, so the instinct transfers; what does not transfer is which English word sits at which distance.
items.explanation_cz: Nejzřetelnějším signálem stylové roviny je v angličtině volba mezi frázovým slovesem a jednoslovným latinského původu. Put off a postpone znamenají totéž, find out a discover znamenají totéž, ale jedno patří do mluvy a do textu, který chce znít jako mluva, a druhé do zprávy, smlouvy nebo dopisu někomu, koho jste nikdy nepotkali. Ani jedno není lepší angličtina. Chybou je jejich míchání — formální dopis, který říká we put off the meeting, nebo rozhovor, v němž zazní I shall investigate it. Čeština rozlišuje tutéž vzdálenost rovněž volbou slov, takže instinkt se přenáší; nepřenáší se to, které anglické slovo v které vzdálenosti stojí.

items.explanation: Formal English replaces short prepositions and conjunctions with longer prepositional phrases: before becomes prior to, because of becomes owing to, if there is becomes in the event of, about becomes regarding or concerning. They are fixed — the noun inside cannot be swapped for a near synonym, and owing to does not become owning to. The one that catches Czech writers is despite: it is a preposition and takes a noun, so despite the delay is right and despite the project was late is not; for a clause English needs although or even though.
items.explanation_cz: Formální angličtina nahrazuje krátké předložky a spojky delšími předložkovými frázemi: z before se stane prior to, z because of owing to, z if there is in the event of, z about regarding nebo concerning. Jsou pevné — jméno uvnitř nelze zaměnit za blízké synonymum a z owing to se nestane owning to. Českým pisatelům dělá potíže despite: je to předložka a váže se se jménem, takže despite the delay je správně, kdežto despite the project was late nikoli; před větu potřebuje angličtina although nebo even though.

Speech measures with a lot, a bit, really and loads of; writing measures with considerably, somewhat, particularly, substantially and a great deal of. cards.title: Register is a choice, not a level
cards.body: Formal English is not better English and informal English is not lazy English. They are two settings, and a competent writer moves between them on purpose. What marks someone out at C1 is not knowing the formal words but keeping one setting for the length of a text: a letter that opens we regret to inform you and closes so give us a shout has not made two small slips, it has made one large one.
cards.body_cz: Formální angličtina není lepší angličtina a neformální angličtina není lajdácká angličtina. Jsou to dvě nastavení a schopný pisatel mezi nimi přechází záměrně. Na úrovni C1 nerozhoduje znalost formálních slov, nýbrž schopnost udržet jedno nastavení po celou délku textu: dopis, který začíná we regret to inform you a končí so give us a shout, neudělal dvě drobné chyby, ale jednu velkou.

cards.title: One word instead of two
cards.body: The clearest single signal is the phrasal verb. Speech prefers put off, find out, set up, look into; writing prefers postpone, discover, establish, investigate. The pairs mean the same thing — the difference is entirely distance. Reach for the single Latinate verb in a report, a contract or a letter to a stranger, and for the phrasal verb everywhere else.
cards.body_cz: Nejzřetelnějším jednotlivým signálem je frázové sloveso. Mluva dává přednost spojením put off, find out, set up, look into; psaný text slovesům postpone, discover, establish, investigate. Dvojice znamenají totéž — rozdíl je čistě ve vzdálenosti. Ve zprávě, smlouvě nebo dopise někomu cizímu sáhněte po jednoslovném latinském slovese, všude jinde po frázovém.
points: The formal verb is usually one word and usually longer — that is the whole pattern.
Both halves are correct English. Only the setting decides.
Do not mix them inside one sentence: we shall look into it sits badly with itself.

cards.title: Longer prepositions
cards.body: Formal writing stretches its prepositions. Before becomes prior to, because of becomes owing to, about becomes regarding or concerning, if there is becomes in the event of. These are fixed phrases: the noun inside cannot be swapped for a synonym, and the small word after it is not free either — prior takes to, in accordance takes with, on behalf takes of.
cards.body_cz: Formální text své předložky natahuje. Z before se stane prior to, z because of owing to, z about regarding nebo concerning, z if there is in the event of. Jsou to pevné fráze: jméno uvnitř nelze nahradit synonymem a ani drobné slovo za ním není volné — prior žádá to, in accordance žádá with, on behalf žádá of.
points: Despite is a preposition: despite the delay, never despite the project was late.
For a clause use although or even though — that is the half Czech writers drop.
With a view to is followed by an -ing form, not an infinitive.

cards.title: The letter frames
cards.body: Official correspondence runs on a short list of frames that are learnt whole and never taken apart. They carry most of the formality on their own, which is why a letter built from them reads as correct even when the sentences between them are plain.
cards.body_cz: Úřední korespondence stojí na krátkém seznamu rámců, které se učí vcelku a nikdy se nerozebírají. Nesou většinu formálnosti samy o sobě, a proto dopis z nich postavený působí správně i tehdy, jsou-li věty mezi nimi prosté.

table.caption: learn them whole
rows: We regret to inform you that…
We would be grateful if you could…
Please do not hesitate to contact us.
I look forward to hearing from you.
We shall contact you in due course.

points: Regret takes the to-infinitive: we regret to inform you.
Look forward to takes -ing — that to is a preposition: hearing, not hear. This is the commonest error in the set.
Kindly and please do the same job; kindly is the more distant of the two.

cards.title: Measuring formally
cards.body: How much is said is a register signal too. Speech measures with a lot, a bit, really and loads of; writing measures with considerably, somewhat, particularly, substantially and a great deal of. Two of these pairs are not a matter of style at all but of grammar, and getting them wrong is an error rather than an informality.
cards.body_cz: Také míra je signálem roviny. Mluva měří slovy a lot, a bit, really a loads of; psaný text slovy considerably, somewhat, particularly, substantially a a great deal of. Dvě z těchto dvojic nejsou vůbec věcí stylu, nýbrž gramatiky, a chyba v nich není neformálnost, ale chyba.

table.caption: the informal measure and its written twin

points: A great deal of and a large amount of take uncountable nouns: a great deal of work.
A large number of takes countable nouns: a large number of clients — never a large amount of clients.
The adverb goes before the adjective it measures and after the verb it measures.

cards.title: Keeping one setting
cards.body: The failure at C1 is almost never a missing formal word — it is a text that changes setting halfway. Read anything you have written for one thing only: does every sentence sound as though it is addressed to the same person? A formal frame followed by a phrasal verb, or a contract sentence with really in the middle of it, is the seam a reader notices even when they could not name what is wrong.
cards.body_cz: Selhání na úrovni C1 téměř nikdy nespočívá v chybějícím formálním slově — spočívá v textu, který v půli změní nastavení. Čtěte si napsané kvůli jediné otázce: zní každá věta, jako by byla adresována téže osobě? Formální rámec následovaný frázovým slovesem nebo smluvní věta s really uprostřed jsou švem, kterého si čtenář všimne, i když by nedokázal pojmenovat, co je špatně.

table.caption: seams a reader hears
rows: We regret to inform you we had to put it off.
Owing to the delay, costs went up a lot.
The board shall look into it.

points: Fix a seam by moving the whole sentence, not the one odd word.
Contractions belong to the informal setting; write them out in the formal one.
When you cannot tell which setting a reader expects, the more distant one is the safer guess.
